schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE R (A INT, B INT);
q1: SELECT COUNT(*) AS A FROM R AS X
q2: SELECT COUNT(Y.B) FROM R AS Y
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS A FROM R AS X
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT COUNT(Y.B) FROM R AS Y
counterexample: INSERT INTO R (A, B) VALUES (1, 10), (2, NULL), (3, NULL);
explanation: Q1 counts the total number of rows in table R, while Q2 counts the number of non-NULL values in column B of table R. They are not equivalent because a table can have rows with NULL values in column B, in which case Q1 would return a higher count than Q2.
counterexample_dsp: A table with 3 rows, where the first and third rows have NULL values in column B, and the second row has a non-NULL value in column B.
